<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap, non-training checks
are fine.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
2. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
3. **Expected effect** — which metric the fix should move and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After you submit the report, the system deletes everything under
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then re-runs the experiment in your
repaired workspace as a foreground process, using the launch script:

```text
examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh
```

with this environment:

```text
LOG_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
WANDB_MODE=offline
WANDB_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
```

The effective run must use:

- HF checkpoint `/workspace/Qwen2.5-3B`
- Megatron torch_dist reference `/workspace/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist`
- train data `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/train.parquet`
- validation data `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/test.parquet`
- `--num-rollout 100`
- `--eval-interval 10`
- local retrieval server `http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve`

**Make sure your repaired launch script actually produces that run.** The
staged `examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh` bakes `--num-rollout 200`
directly into the training invocation with no environment override, and the
graded rerun passes no budget override either — if you leave 200 in place,
the rerun blows its time budget and scores 0. Edit the script to the required
100.

Two more traps specific to this task:

- **Log placement is your script's job.** The launch script builds the Ray
  runtime-env JSON itself and only propagates a few variables into the
  training process — `WANDB_DIR` set in the environment does **not** reach it.
  Your repaired script must itself write the training log and the offline
  W&B data under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` (offline W&B below
  `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/wandb`), or the grader will find no
  metrics to grade.
- **The W&B key.** The script passes `--wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}` unquoted;
  offline mode gets a harmless local placeholder from the environment, so the
  script must not choke when it is a placeholder rather than a real key.

A task-specific grading script then reads **only this fresh run's** files
under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` and scores the key metrics; logs
written anywhere else are ignored. Do not copy, edit, or fabricate log
metrics. Otherwise the run is scored 0.

I’ll inspect the launch path, training and evaluation evidence, and the data and reward code, then repair any supported defects. I’ll use only non-training checks and write the report to `/workspace/report.md`.

The default\n# soft limit (1024) is far too low and the rollout crashes with\n# \"OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files\". Raise it as high as the hard limit\n# allows; ray workers launched below inherit this shell's limit.\nulimit -n \"$(ulimit -Hn)\"\n\n# will prevent ray from buffering stdout/stderr\nexport PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1\n\n# Online W&B initialization is unreliable from this devspace and a timeout\n# kills the RolloutManager actor. Default to local logging; callers can opt in\n# with WANDB_MODE=online once network access is stable.\nexport WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}\n\n# The persistent faiss retriever (--faiss_gpu) holds ~9GB more on GPU0 than on the\n# other GPUs, so SGLang's TP memory-balance check (\"memory capacity is unbalanced\")\n# fatally aborts the GPU0-paired engine on restart. The imbalance is expected and\n# within the mem-fraction-static headroom. This export\n# only covers the driver/train side and is kept as defense-in-depth.\nexport SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0\n\n# On the cybertron devspaces an egress whitelist proxy is exported into every\n# shell (http_proxy/https_proxy -> whitelist-proxy:7891) with a no_proxy that\n# does NOT cover localhost or this node. ray's \"ray job submit\" then routes its\n# request to the local dashboard (127.0.0.1:8265) through that proxy and gets a\n# 502 Bad Gateway, and the same happens for sglang's node-local HTTP. Prepend\n# the loopback addresses, this node's IP and its /16 to no_proxy so all\n# in-cluster / on-node traffic bypasses the proxy. Harmless off-cluster (the\n# vars are simply absent). hostname -I is the reliable source for the node IP;\n# `ip` is not always on PATH in these non-login shells, so it is only a fallback.\nNODE_IP=$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') || true\nif [ -z \"${NODE_IP:-}\" ]; then\n   NODE_IP=$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i==\"src\"){print $(i+1); exit}}') || true\nfi\ncase \"${NODE_IP:-}\" in\n   *.*.*.*)\n      PREFIX16=$(echo \"$NODE_IP\" | awk -F. '{print $1\".\"$2\".0.0/16\"}')\n      export no_proxy=\"127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0,${NODE_IP},${PREFIX16}${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}\"\n      export NO_PROXY=\"$no_proxy\" ;;\n   *)\n      export no_proxy=\"127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}\"\n      export NO_PROXY=\"$no_proxy\" ;;\nesac\n\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd -- \"$(dirname -- \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" &>/dev/null && pwd)\"\n# slime repo root (this recipe lives at <slime>/examples/search-r1)\nSLIME_DIR=\"$(cd -- \"${SCRIPT_DIR}/../..\" &>/dev/null && pwd)\"\nsource \"${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../scripts/models/qwen2.5-3B.sh\"\n\n# Use the HuggingFace mirror for all downloads.\nexport HF_ENDPOINT=${HF_ENDPOINT:-https://hf-mirror.com}\n\nDATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}\nMODEL_DIR=${MODEL_DIR:-$PWD}\nbash \"$SCRIPT_DIR/prepare_data.sh\"\n\nDATASET_DIR=${DATASET_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/nq_hotpotqa_train}\nTRAIN_DATA=${TRAIN_DATA:-$DATASET_DIR/train.parquet}\nTEST_DATA=${TEST_DATA:-$DATASET_DIR/test.parquet}\n\n# Model checkpoints under MODEL_DIR: the HF checkpoint and its mcore\n# (torch_dist) conversion used as the reference weights.\nHF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B}\nDIST_MODEL_DIR=${DIST_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist}\n\n# Download the HF checkpoint if it is not already present under MODEL_DIR.\nif [ ! -d \"$HF_MODEL_DIR\" ] || [ -z \"$(ls -A \"$HF_MODEL_DIR\" 2>/dev/null)\" ]; then\n   echo \"[model] $HF_MODEL_DIR missing; downloading Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B from $HF_ENDPOINT\"\n   hf download Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B --local-dir \"$HF_MODEL_DIR\"\nfi\n\n# Convert to a torch_dist (mcore) checkpoint if not already done.\nif [ ! -d \"$DIST_MODEL_DIR\" ] || [ -z \"$(ls -A \"$DIST_MODEL_DIR\" 2>/dev/null)\" ]; then\n   echo \"[model] converting $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $DIST_MODEL_DIR (torch_dist)\"\n   PYTHONPATH=${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM} python \"${SLIME_DIR}/tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py\" \\\n      \"${MODEL_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n      --hf-checkpoint \"$HF_MODEL_DIR\" \\\n      --save \"$DIST_MODEL_DIR\"\nfi\n\nCKPT_ARGS=(\n   --hf-checkpoint \"$HF_MODEL_DIR\"\n   --ref-load \"$DIST_MODEL_DIR\"\n   # --load \"$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_slime/\"\n   --save \"$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_slime/\"\n   --save-interval 10\n)\n\n# --- the local dense retrieval server ---------------------------------------\n# generate_with_search.py posts every search turn to\n# http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve, so the rollout cannot start without it.\n#\n# Started here rather than left to the caller, because none of the three paths\n# that run this script are able to start it themselves:\n#\n#   * the harness's prepare stage is a container created and removed around\n#     prepare.sh (evaluation/evaluator.py::_run_prepare, and\n#     runtimes/providers/docker.py::close_sandbox is a `docker rm -f`), so a\n#     server backgrounded there does not outlive the stage -- and prepare is\n#     waited on in the foreground, so starting it there without detaching just\n#     hangs until the stage timeout;\n#   * on the harbor path prepare can be a build-time RUN layer, which has no\n#     GPU at all;\n#   * the solution-level instruction forbids the agent from using `&`, nohup,\n#     tmux, screen or any other detach mechanism.\n#\n# A child of this script is none of those things: the script itself still runs\n# in the foreground and still owns the exit status. Only whitespace is allowed between tags\n                if part.strip():\n                    return False, f\"Unexpected content '{part.strip()}' between tags (state: {state})\"\n            else:\n                return False, f\"Unexpected content in state {state}\"\n\n    # 0.3\n            else:\n                return structure_format_score  # 0.2\n        else:\n            return 0\n    else:\n        if em_check(answer, ground_truth[\"target\"]):\n            if is_valid_format:\n                return score  # 1\n            else:\n                return score - structure_format_score  # 0.8\n        elif is_valid_format:\n            if retrieval_correct:\n                return structure_format_score + retrieval_score  # 0.3\n            else:\n                return structure_format_score  # 0.2\n        else:\n            return final_format_score  # 0.1\n"}'}]

+**Assessment: unhealthy.** The run learns some held-out QA, but its search trajectories use an incorrect optimization mask. The defect is reproducible without training. The frozen evidence supports impaired search learning and a low validation plateau; it does not establish how much accuracy this single repair will recover.
+
+**Root cause and evidence.** In `examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py`, the generator appended `1` to its local `loss_mask` for every retrieved passage or invalid-action feedback token. `Sample.append_response_tokens(..., trainable=False)` correctly appended zeros to the sample, but the generator overwrote that mask with its local copy before returning. Consequently, environment text was treated as if it had been sampled by the policy.
+
+`slime/ray/rollout.py` passes this final mask into the training batch and calculates loss denominators from it. `slime/backends/megatron_utils/loss.py` uses the mask-based reducer for policy loss, entropy, and reference KL; `cp_utils.get_sum_of_sample_mean` includes every unmasked token in its numerator and denominator. Long retrieved passages therefore receive policy credit/blame and dilute the action-token contribution. Their stored rollout log probabilities are dummy zeros, which also contaminate masked train/rollout log-probability comparisons. TIS and rollout-logprob optimization are disabled in the effective configuration, so I do not attribute this run's policy ratios to those dummy values.
+
+A mocked search → observation → answer execution of the original function produced 100 model-generated tokens and 65 observation tokens. All 165 were reported as effective training tokens, including all 65 observation tokens. With the repair, only the 100 generated tokens are trainable; the passage remains in the next inference request and in the complete trajectory.
+
+The historical observations come from `wandb/latest-run/files/output.log`, cross-checked against `historical_evidence/eval_scores.json`, `historical_evidence/manifest.json`, and `outputs/metrics.json`:
+
+| Evaluation step | Held-out `eval/nq_test` | Reported mean response length | Truncated fraction |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| 0 | 0.048000 | 1568.610 | 0.381333 |
+| 29 | 0.104667 | 78.854 | 0.013000 |
+| 69 | 0.158667 | 14.413 | 0.000333 |
+| 99 | 0.154333 | 15.056 | 0.000667 |
+| 199 | 0.164667 | 9.763 | 0.000000 |
+
+Held-out accuracy genuinely improves initially, but remains around 15–16% after step 69 while responses become extremely short. Training raw reward rises from 0.039063 at rollout 0 to 0.160156 at 99 and 0.167969 at 199. Training response length falls from 1751.461 to 9.637 by rollout 99; its median is already 9 tokens at rollout 30. This is consistent with a move toward direct answers and little search. Short responses and falling truncation alone would not establish a defect; the demonstrated mask error supplies the concrete mechanism.
+
+Every one of the 200 recorded rollouts has identical `perf/tokens_per_gpu_per_sec` and `perf/effective_tokens_per_gpu_per_sec`. The metric implementation uses full response length for the former and `sum(loss_mask)` for the latter. At rollout 0 both are 2228.487 despite a 13,912-token maximum trajectory. This corroborates counting observations as training tokens. Mean rollout time falls from 22.63 seconds in rollouts 0–9 to 3.14 seconds in 60–99 alongside the length collapse. That speedup and near-zero late truncation do not establish successful retrieval reasoning.
+
+The recorded configuration uses GRPO, 32 prompts × 8 samples, learning rate 1e-6, KL-loss coefficient 0.001, and clipping 0.2/0.28. Approximately 23 of 32 prompt groups remain all-zero-reward groups on average in rollouts 60–99. Near-zero mean advantages are expected after group centering. Logged `rollout/kl=0` follows `kl_coef=0` in advantage computation; it does not mean the separately enabled KL loss is absent. The frozen output contains no gradient-norm, policy-loss, or optimizer-step traces, so it cannot support claims about gradient explosions or optimizer stability. I left those settings unchanged.
+
+Data and reward checks found 169,615 training rows and 11,015 validation rows, nonempty prompts and answer targets, and zero exact question overlap between splits after lowercasing and whitespace normalization. The unchanged first 3,000 validation rows are NQ. The prompt includes an example answer, explaining why the scorer expects more than one answer-tag pair in the concatenated prompt/response. Although `format_score=0.2` is passed, the scorer's active structure/final/retrieval bonuses default to zero: this run's reward is binary exact match. Reward semantics, labels, data order, validation slice, and frozen evidence were preserved. The local client requests `return_scores=False`, matching the server's flat document response; its parsing was not changed. Infrastructure upload errors in `experiment_logs/cybertron-751761.log` do not explain the completed sequence of training/evaluation records.
+
+There were also concrete rerun defects: the staged launcher specified 200 rollouts, did not capture its training output under the required results directory, and omitted W&B mode/directory from its Ray runtime environment. These would violate the stated rerun budget and metric-discovery contract independently of learning quality.
+
+**Files changed.**
+
+| File | Change |
+| --- | --- |
+| `examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py` | Set the local observation/feedback loss mask to zero and explain why it must agree with `trainable=False`. Keep generated tokens trainable and retain all context and aligned token/log-probability metadata. |
+| `examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh` | Set `--num-rollout 100`; retain `--eval-interval 10`. Pin HF, reference, train, and test paths to the required `/workspace` assets and run from the repository directory. Pin retrieval readiness to port 8000. Capture stdout/stderr in `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/train.log`, with the retrieval log in the same directory. Set W&B's root directory to that directory, so offline data goes beneath its `wandb/` child. Pass W&B mode/directory both as CLI arguments and Ray environment variables. Generate correctly escaped runtime JSON; propagate unbuffered output and local proxy exclusions; include repository imports. Quote all argument arrays and the driver path, preserving the existing `WANDB_API_KEY`/`EMPTY` fallback as one argument. Enable pipeline failure propagation. |
+| `examples/search-r1/test_generate_with_search.py` | Add four CPU regression tests with mocked inference and retrieval: search/observation/answer, invalid-action feedback, direct answers, and truncation. Check context retention, exact mask boundaries, token/log-probability/top-p alignment, stop tags, and unchanged correct/incorrect reward outcomes. |
+| `report.md` | Add this diagnosis, change inventory, validation, and expected effects. |
+
+The effective launch uses `/workspace/Qwen2.5-3B`, `/workspace/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist`, `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/train.parquet`, and `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/test.parquet@[0:3000]`. Retrieval remains `http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve`. The reference conversion directory is absent in the snapshot; the existing foreground conversion branch remains available to the system's launch. I did not run conversion or training.
+
+**Checks performed.** All four regression tests passed using `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m unittest discover -s examples/search-r1 -p test_generate_with_search.py -v`. Shell syntax and Python AST checks passed. The actual CPU loss-reduction function was checked in isolation: changing only observation-token loss values leaves the reduced action loss unchanged. An assignment-only shell check extracted the launcher's arrays and JSON, replaced submission with an argument printer, and validated the required settings from an unrelated working directory with conflicting path variables. It passed with an ordinary placeholder W&B key, a placeholder containing spaces, and an unset key, including JSON escaping for a results path containing spaces and quotes. No launch script, Ray service, retriever, W&B run, inference, or training process was started; no historical metrics were copied or edited.
+
+**Expected effect.** The main target is higher held-out `eval/nq_test` at the 100-rollout horizon, compared with the historical step-99 value of 0.154333, by concentrating optimization on generated reasoning, search queries, and answers. On identical trajectories, effective-token counts decrease by exactly the observation-token count; effective throughput becomes lower than total-token throughput when retrieval is used, correcting prior overcounting. Masked train/rollout log-probability discrepancy should lose the contribution from dummy observation probabilities. Successful search may produce longer trajectories and take more rollout time than the collapsed late baseline; longer output is useful only if held-out accuracy improves. No specific reduction below the already near-zero late truncation rate is promised. The 100-rollout budget reduces scheduled training work, and explicit log routing makes fresh evaluation and training metrics discoverable. Accuracy gains remain to be measured by the system's rerun.
*** End Patch"));

steps.message:
The experiment is unhealthy: retrieved passages were incorrectly included in the training loss.

Fixed the observation mask, required 100-rollout configuration, and log routing. Four CPU regression tests and launch-argument checks passed. No training was launched.

Report: [report.md](/workspace/report.md)
